summary: Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology. He studied at Indiana University and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair, Ludo Rocher, and Gregory Schopen. He served as Associate Professor at Cornell University (attested 2000–2008).

Daniel Clarke Waugh works in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Yale University and Harvard University, and held an academic post at the University of Washington from circa 1972 to 2009.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Cambridge. He served at Yale and UC Berkeley, was President of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901) and Carnegie Institution (ca. 1902–1904), and headed the American Oriental Society (1893–1906).

Daniel Cozort works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional Tibetan teachers. He taught at Bates College (~1987–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988–2021).

Daniel Dubuisson specializes in religious studies and Indology. He has held positions at University Lille-III, and served as director of research at both the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique and the University of Lille (attested 2010).

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Harvard University under Willard Van Orman Quine and Walter Eugene Clark, and under Kalipada Tarkacharya. He was Harvard's Wales Professor of Sanskrit from circa 1958 until retiring emeritus in 1983.

Daniel John Gogerly worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as chairman of the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society from circa 1838 to 1862 and was president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka from circa 1856 to 1862.

Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied at the University of Chicago (~1963–1971). He held posts at Oberlin College (~1970–1973) and the University of British Columbia, serving as department head (~1985–1993) and professor.

Daniel M. Stuart specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley, mentored by Alexander von Rospatt and others, and was Assistant Professor at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017).

Daniel R. Tuzzeo specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his graduate thesis at Florida State University, where he studied under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Stuart Capper, Jr. works in religious studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Virginia under Robert Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (attested 2000).

Daniel Veidlinger is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as a research associate at Chiang Mai University (1999), and held a post at California State University, Chico.

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, where he was attested as an instructor in 2010, the same year he held an instructorship at Mary Baldwin University.

Daniela Berti works in Indology and ethno-anthropology. She earned her Ph.D. in Research Methodology in Ethno-Anthropology at the University of Siena and was attested as a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya in 2004.

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned doctorates from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and served as a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).
Danielle Feller is an Indologist who completed her Ph.D. in 2001 at the University of Lausanne, studying under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst and teacher Ganesh Umakant Thite.

Daoquan Yu was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Cheeloo University and under Jacques Bacot in the 1930s, later serving as professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China from circa 1953 to 1992.

Daud Ali specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at William & Mary and the University of Chicago (~1986–1996), and held academic appointments at SOAS University of London and the University of Pennsylvania (circa 2009).
David A. Dilworth is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo, and held an academic post at Stony Brook University from circa 1970 to 2012.

David A. Hall specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shoshin Ichishima and earned a doctorate from UC Berkeley (1990). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).
